corrected_value.title: A genome-wide association study for myopia and refractive error identifies a susceptibility locus at 15q25.

decisions.location: Introduction, paragraph 2; Methods and Results (15q25 results); Reference 14
decisions.quote: Two recent genome-wide association studies (GWASs) identified strong association with refractive error in two locations on chromosome 15. Solouki et al. [ 11 ] reported an association on 15q14 that was subsequently replicated in several other populations [ 12 , 13 ]. Hysi et al. [ 14 ] published a second locus on 15q25 at the same time.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (never previously adjudicated). The primary full text empirically retests two distinct published chromosome 15 refractive-error GWAS discovery findings in the AREDS cohort (n=1,877/1,879): the 15q14 association of Solouki et al. (2010, reference [11], doi:10.1038/ng.663) and the 15q25 association of Hysi et al. (2010, reference [14], doi:10.1038/ng.664). For 15q25, the authors use Hysi et al.'s reported effect sizes (beta=-0.35, OR=1.16) for power calculations, test the 15q25 discovery SNP rs8027411, the CREAM replication SNPs, custom TaqMan tagging SNPs, and 1,224 array SNPs within 350 kb of rs8027411 against quantitative spherical equivalent, myopia, and hyperopia, and compare the non-replication of the original SNPs with significant regional association for hyperopia at rs7164400 (p=8.39x10^-4). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 2530, doi:10.1038/ng.663) represents only the companion Solouki et al. (2010) 15q14 discovery study (also coded as sibling target_index 0). Report equivalence does not apply because Hysi et al. (2010, Nat Genet 42:902-905) and Solouki et al. (2010, Nat Genet 42:897-901) are separate GWAS articles discovering different chromosomal loci (15q25 vs. 15q14) with different lead variants and discovery cohorts. Note that the intervening CREAM meta-analysis (Verhoeven et al., 2012, reference [15]) already included the AREDS cohort and is used here only for SNP selection context rather than as an independent target.
